tagline: See your site on an iPhone or a Pixel, tomorrow morning, in Arabic or in dark mode, from a panel inside the page
hero_hint: The knobs handle on the edge of this page is devknobs itself. Press [[⇧K]] or click it, then pick a phone. Drag it across to move the panel to the other edge.
stage_line: Open the panel with [[⇧K]] and move a knob. The card with its name shows what the page reads now.
contrast_sample: This gray line gets stronger with more contrast
transparency_sample: Half of this line sits under a see-through plate, which turns solid
vision_line: Pick a vision filter and some of these colors look the same
text_sample: This line is set at 1 rem
knob_time: clock · time zone · send to server
debug_line: Push a box past the edge, then turn on overflow to mark it. Outlines draws a line around every box.
debug_push: Push a box past the edge
debug_box: This box is wider than the viewport
pick_line: Press [[⇧G]] for grab, or open inspect, and pick one of these.
pick_box: A margin of 12 pixels, a border of 4 and a padding of 12
pick_font: AAA is a web font, the rest is its fallback
pick_media: This line is gray on a narrow screen and darker on a wide one
pick_inherit_parent: This line sets a font and
how_frame: Pick a device and your page loads again in a same-origin frame the size of the viewport that device gives a page. Media queries, innerWidth, vw units and fixed elements all see a real viewport.
how_patch: The other knobs change what your code reads: media queries, matchMedia, Date, Intl, navigator.language, geolocation and the user agent. Your CSS and your JavaScript see the same thing.
how_setup: One script tag or one import. No browser extension, no CSS to add, no code to change. Load it in development only.
feature_devices_detail: iPhone 18 Pro back to SE, the folding iPhone Duo, Pixel 10 and 9, iPads, laptops and desktops. Phones wear their real body, with Safari or Chrome drawn around your page and bars that shrink as you scroll.
feature_touch_detail: Inside a phone, your mouse acts as a finger: touch events, drag to scroll, no hover. Find the menu that only opens on a mouse hover event.
feature_time_detail: Set the clock to next Friday or run it 60 times faster. Change the time zone and the position geolocation reports. Send the time to your own dev server in a header.
feature_language_detail: Any locale with its writing direction, for Intl and navigator.language. Pseudo-localized text, accented and padded, to see where longer words break your layout. A bigger default text size.
feature_look_detail: Dark mode, more contrast, reduced motion and color blindness filters. Slow CSS animations and transitions down, pause them, or replay them from the start.
feature_debug_detail: Mark every box that makes the page scroll sideways. Outline every element. Swap the user agent, or tell the page it is offline.
layers_line: The touch pointer stays on top of what the page opens
layers_dialog_title: A dialog in the top layer
layers_dialog_try: Pick a phone in the panel and your mouse becomes a touch dot. Move it over this dialog: the dot stays above it.
layers_dialog_fields: The dot leaves text fields and sliders to the browser, so you can type and drag here as usual.
layers_popover_text: A popover is in the top layer too, and a click outside closes it
features_panel: The panel works from the keyboard: open it and type a knob's name. It lists the knobs you set, and its footer shows five shortcuts. Each one can be set to another key in the panel's settings.
features_readme: Every knob and how it works, in the README
tour_pick: Pick an element on the page
tour_copied: Copied, ready to paste into your AI chat
try_invalid: Enter a web address that starts with http or https
try_works: Device, rotation and mat work here. Knobs that change the page need devknobs installed in your project
try_refused: Many sites do not allow being shown inside another page. Install devknobs in your own project and every knob works
try_local: A local site shows only when its dev server allows being shown inside another page
new_duo: The iPhone Duo, shut on its cover screen or open on its inner one. It folds in 3D, in frames rendered from Apple's own model in a scene adapted from
new_mat: Six colors for the mat under the frame: blue, green, magenta, purple, red and graphite. A new one splashes out from behind the device.
new_motion: A new device and a rotation animate in view, with the device turning on the mat.
new_settings: Settings behind the gear: set any shortcut to another key, or hide the handle while the panel is closed.
new_sides: The panel sits on either edge of the window. Drag or fling the handle across, and a new tab opens it where you left it.
new_keys: New default keys: [[⇧K]] for the panel, [[⇧G]] for grab and [[⇧R]] to replay animations.
grab_title: Grab an element for your coding agent
grab_intro: Press [[⇧G]] and point at the page. A box sits on the element under the pointer, with a label that shows its tag and its React component. Click, and the element goes to your clipboard. A check and "Copied" show next to it.
grab_try: Try it here: press [[⇧G]], point at the knobs headline at the top of this page, click, then paste. This live site runs React's production build, so here the line names short, minified components and a selector. In your own dev server you get files and lines, like this:
grab_example_label: What the clipboard gets for that headline, with this site running in development
grab_example_code:
[

knobs

in Landing (at src/routes/index.tsx:745:9) in RootComponent (at src/routes/__root.tsx:65:7)]
grab_context: One line per element: its HTML, the component it is written in with the file, line and column of its JSX, then the components that rendered it, up to three components of your own in all. Library code stays out. Paste the line into your agent and it can find the code.
grab_key_copy: [[⇧G]] again turns grab off. In a text field of the page, [[⇧G]] types a capital G as always.
grab_key_arrows: [[↑]] goes to the parent, [[↓]] to the first child, [[←]] and [[→]] to the elements beside it. [[Enter]] or [[C]] copies.
grab_key_shift: [[Shift]] and a click gather several elements, one line each.
grab_key_escape: [[Esc]] leaves without copying. The page's own click and hover handlers never hear the clicks grab takes.
grab_lines: For a file and line on every component, React has to report to a devtools hook from its first render. The React devtools extension has one, and the early script puts one in place. Without either, grab may only name the components and fall back to a selector.
grab_frame: Grab works on the page inside a phone frame too. The box color is a knob: auto, blue, green, pink, orange, purple or cyan.
grab_replace: Already using react-grab? devknobs writes the same line format and the same clipboard type, and grabKey: "meta+c" keeps react-grab's key. Remove react-grab and you have one dev tool less.
grab_api_label: Another key, no grab, or a grab from code

usage_react_note: In Next.js, gate the import itself with next/dynamic. A static import stays in the production bundle, even behind the check.
usage_early_note: Add it when your page reads a media query, the time or the user agent while it boots. It also lets grab name the file and line of every component.
limits_ua: There is no extension, so some things are emulated in the page. Your server still gets the real User-Agent header.
limits_touch: CSS :hover still follows the real mouse. Touch is one finger, with no pinch and no long press menu.
limits_phone: env(safe-area-inset-*) stays 0. There is no keyboard, and Safari's tabs and share sheet do not open.
limits_clock: The clock moves the time the page reads, not timers. setTimeout and performance.now keep real time.
limits_devtools: Forced colors, print and real network throttling still need the browser devtools.
limits_bezels: The iPhone and Pixel bezel images belong to Apple and Google and are not under the MIT license.
